preamble.summary: The Vulgate's chapter 12 continues the banquet scene and transitions into the pivotal moment. With Holofernes passed out from wine and all his servants dismissed, Judith finds herself alone with the unconscious general in his tent. The stage is set for the act that defines the entire book.
preamble.remarkable: Jerome's Vulgate compresses the Greek text significantly in these transitional chapters. The narrative tension builds through simplicity — servants depart, silence falls, and Judith stands alone with her enemy and her God.
preamble.friction: The chapter division in the Vulgate does not align precisely with the Greek or other versions, making cross-reference challenging. Jerome's rapid translation produced a leaner, more dramatic text.
preamble.connections: The scene of a lone woman with a sleeping enemy echoes Ruth at the threshing floor (Ruth 3) and Jael with Sisera (Judges 4:17-21) — but with far higher stakes.

verses.text_latin: Ut autem sero factum est festinaverunt servi illius ad hospitia sua et conclusit Vagao ostia cubiculi et abiit.
verses.rendering: When evening had come, his servants hurried to their quarters, and Bagoas closed the doors of the bedchamber and departed.

verses.text_latin: Erant autem omnes fatigati a vino.
verses.rendering: They were all heavy with wine.
translator_notes: A devastatingly simple sentence — the entire Assyrian camp is drunk and vulnerable. The mighty army undone by its own indulgence.

key_terms.note: The empire's wine-stupor contrasts with Israel's desperate thirst for water — a moral inversion.

verses.text_latin: Eratque Iudith sola in cubiculo.
verses.rendering: And Judith was alone in the bedchamber.
translator_notes: Five words in Latin — perhaps the most charged sentence in the book. She is alone with the unconscious enemy, the closed door, and God.

verses.text_latin: Porro Holofernes iacebat in lecto nimia ebrietate sopitus.
verses.rendering: Holofernes lay on his bed, sunk in deep drunken sleep.

key_terms.note: Sopitus suggests not merely sleep but stupor — he is beyond waking, beyond defense, beyond agency.

verses.text_latin: Dixitque Iudith puellae suae ut staret foris ante cubiculum et observaret.
verses.rendering: Judith told her maidservant to stand outside the bedchamber and keep watch.

verses.text_latin: Stetitque Iudith ante lectum orans cum lacrimis et labiorum motu in silentio.
verses.rendering: Judith stood before the bed, praying with tears and with the silent movement of her lips.
translator_notes: Silent prayer before the act — her lips move without sound, like Hannah's prayer (1 Samuel 1:13). The killing is framed as worship.

key_terms.rendered_as: the silent movement of her lips
key_terms.note: Echoes Hannah's silent prayer (1 Samuel 1:13) — marking this as a sacred, not merely violent, moment.

verses.text_latin: Dicens confirma me Domine Deus Israhel et respice in hac hora ad opera manuum mearum ut sicut promisisti Hierusalem civitatem tuam erigas et hoc quod credens per te posse fieri cogitavi perficiam.
verses.rendering: She said: Strengthen me, Lord God of Israel, and look in this hour upon the work of my hands, so that as you promised, you may raise up Jerusalem your city, and that what I have planned, believing it could be accomplished through you, I may bring to completion.

key_terms.note: A warrior's prayer for divine empowerment before the decisive blow.

verses.text_latin: Et cum haec dixisset accessit ad columnam quae erat ad caput lectuli eius et pugionem eius qui in ea ligatus pendebat exsolvit.
verses.rendering: When she had said this, she approached the column at the head of his bed and loosed his short sword, which hung tied to it.
translator_notes: She uses his own weapon — fulfilling her prayer of 9:12 ('Let his own sword cut off his pride'). The detail is both tactically precise and theologically loaded.

key_terms.note: His own blade becomes the instrument of his destruction — the ultimate ironic reversal.

verses.text_latin: Cumque evaginasset illum adprehendit comam capitis eius et ait confirma me Domine Deus in hac hora.
verses.rendering: When she had drawn it from its sheath, she seized the hair of his head and said: Strengthen me, Lord God, in this hour.
translator_notes: The second 'confirma me' — she prays again at the moment of contact. The act is sustained by prayer from beginning to end.

verses.text_latin: Et percussit bis in cervicem eius et abscidit caput eius et abstulit conopeum eius a columnis et evolvit corpus eius truncum.
verses.rendering: She struck twice at his neck and cut off his head. She pulled down his canopy from the pillars and rolled his headless body off the bed.
translator_notes: Two strikes — not a single clean blow. The detail is realistic and humanizing: she is a widow, not a trained warrior. The effort makes the feat more, not less, remarkable.

key_terms.note: The realistic detail of two blows emphasizes that this is a mortal woman's act empowered by God, not a superhuman feat.

verses.text_latin: Et post pusillum exivit et tradidit caput Holofernis ancillae suae et iussit ut mitteret illud in peram suam.
verses.rendering: After a short while she went out and handed the head of Holofernes to her maidservant, and ordered her to put it in her food bag.
translator_notes: The head goes into the pera — the provisions bag. The container that held kosher food now holds the trophy of holy war. The ordinary vessel repurposed for extraordinary victory.

key_terms.note: The mundane sack becomes the vessel of triumph — an utterly practical and deliberately unheroic detail.

verses.text_latin: Et exierunt duae secundum consuetudinem suam quasi ad orationem et transierunt castra et gyratae vallem venerunt ad portam civitatis.
verses.rendering: The two of them went out according to their custom as if going to prayer, and passing through the camp and circling through the valley, they came to the gate of the city.
translator_notes: Her established routine of nightly prayer excursions now serves as perfect cover. The spiritual discipline was tactical preparation all along.

key_terms.note: The nightly prayer habit she established is now her escape route — piety as strategy.

verses.text_latin: Et dixit Iudith a longe custodibus portarum aperite portas quoniam nobiscum est Deus qui fecit virtutem in Israhel.
verses.rendering: From a distance, Judith called to the gatekeepers: Open the gates! For God is with us — he who has wrought mighty deeds in Israel!

key_terms.note: An Immanuel declaration — the theological conclusion of the entire mission.

verses.text_latin: Et factum est cum audissent viri vocem eius vocaverunt presbyteros civitatis.
verses.rendering: When the men heard her voice, they summoned the elders of the city.

verses.text_latin: Et concurrerunt ad eam omnes a minimo usque ad maximum quoniam sperabant eam iam non esse venturam.
verses.rendering: Everyone ran to her, from the least to the greatest, for they had given up hope that she would return.

verses.text_latin: Et accendentes luminaria congyraverunt circa eam universi illa autem ascendens in eminentiorem locum iussit fieri silentium cumque omnes tacuissent.
verses.rendering: Lighting torches, they all gathered around her. She climbed to a higher place and commanded silence, and when all were quiet,

verses.text_latin: Dixit Iudith laudate Dominum Deum nostrum qui non deseruit sperantes in se.
verses.rendering: Judith said: Praise the Lord our God, who has not forsaken those who hope in him.

key_terms.rendered_as: has not forsaken those who hope in him
key_terms.note: The direct answer to Achior's thesis (5:25) and the people's despair (7:22).

verses.text_latin: Et in me ancillam suam adimplevit misericordiam suam quam promisit domui Israhel et interfecit in manu mea hostem populi sui hac nocte.
verses.rendering: In me, his handmaid, he has fulfilled the mercy he promised to the house of Israel, and by my hand he has slain the enemy of his people this night.

verses.text_latin: Et proferens caput Holofernis de pera ostendit illis dicens ecce caput Holofernis principis militiae Assyriorum et ecce conopeum illius in quo recumbebat in ebrietate sua ubi per manum feminae percussit illum Dominus Deus noster.
verses.rendering: Drawing the head of Holofernes from the bag, she showed it to them, saying: Behold the head of Holofernes, commander of the Assyrian army! And behold his canopy, under which he lay in his drunkenness, where the Lord our God struck him down by the hand of a woman.
translator_notes: The public display of the head is both proof and proclamation. The canopy — symbol of his luxury and power — is now trophy evidence of his fall.

key_terms.rendered_as: by the hand of a woman
key_terms.note: The fulfillment of her prayer (9:15) — God's memorial accomplished through female agency.

verses.text_latin: Vivit autem ipse Dominus quoniam custodivit me angelus eius et hinc euntem et ibi commorantem et inde huc revertentem et non permisit me Dominus ancillam suam coinquinari sed sine pollutione peccati revocavit me vobis gaudentem in victoria sua in evasione mea et in liberatione vestra.
verses.rendering: As the Lord himself lives, his angel has guarded me going out from here and dwelling there and returning here again. The Lord did not permit me, his handmaid, to be defiled, but without the stain of sin he has brought me back to you — rejoicing in his victory, in my escape, and in your deliverance.
translator_notes: Judith declares that her sexual purity was maintained throughout — a critical point for the narrative's moral framework. Her virtue was never compromised despite the dangerous proximity to Holofernes.

key_terms.note: Explicit confirmation that Judith was not sexually violated — the narrative's moral integrity preserved.

verses.text_latin: Confitemini illi omnes quoniam bonus quoniam in saeculum misericordia eius.
verses.rendering: Give thanks to him, all of you, for he is good — for his mercy endures forever.
translator_notes: The liturgical formula of Psalm 136 (118 Vulgate) — Judith's announcement becomes doxology.

key_terms.note: The great refrain of Psalm 136, transforming a military report into worship.

verses.text_latin: Universi autem adorantes Dominum dixerunt ad eam benedixit te Dominus in virtute sua quia per te ad nihilum redegit inimicos nostros.
verses.rendering: All of them, worshipping the Lord, said to her: The Lord has blessed you by his power, because through you he has brought our enemies to nothing.

verses.text_latin: Porro Ozias princeps populi Israhel dixit ad eam benedicta es tu filia a Domino Deo excelso prae omnibus mulieribus super terram.
verses.rendering: Then Uzziah, prince of the people of Israel, said to her: Blessed are you, daughter, by the Lord God Most High, above all women upon the earth.
translator_notes: This blessing directly anticipates Elizabeth's blessing of Mary in Luke 1:42 ('Blessed are you among women'). The typological link between Judith and Mary is rooted in this verse.

key_terms.latin: benedicta es tu filia a Domino Deo excelso prae omnibus mulieribus super terram
key_terms.rendered_as: Blessed are you, daughter, by the Lord God Most High, above all women upon the earth
key_terms.note: The prototype of Elizabeth's greeting to Mary (Luke 1:42) — one of the strongest Judith-Mary typological connections.

verses.text_latin: Benedictus Dominus qui creavit caelum et terram qui te direxit in vulnera capitis principis inimicorum nostrorum.
verses.rendering: Blessed be the Lord who created heaven and earth, who directed you to wound the head of the prince of our enemies.

key_terms.note: An echo of Genesis 3:15 (the protoevangelium) — the woman striking the head of the enemy.

verses.text_latin: Quia hodie nomen tuum ita magnificavit ut non recedat laus tua de ore hominum qui memores fuerint virtutis Domini in aeternum pro quibus non pepercisti animae tuae propter angustias et tribulationem generis tui sed subvenisti ruinae ante conspectum Dei nostri.
verses.rendering: For today he has so magnified your name that your praise shall not depart from the mouths of those who remember the Lord's power forever — because you did not spare your own life on account of the distress and tribulation of your people, but rescued them from ruin before the face of our God.

verses.text_latin: Et dixit omnis populus fiat fiat.
verses.rendering: And all the people said: So be it! So be it!
